0.0.n: Here, 怪異 names a category of supernatural creatures, rather than simply strange events.

0.2.n: Introduces specific examples of the category just mentioned.

0.3.n: Japanese nouns do not mark singular or plural; here it refers to vampires as a type.

0.4.n: Follows an example to show the list is not exhaustive.

0.6.n: Another example in the list, followed by とか.

0.7.n: Repeating とか after examples keeps the list open-ended.

0.9.n: 鬼 refers to creatures from Japanese folklore, often depicted with horns.

0.10.n: This と is the first part of とか, split across two word entries; it is not acting alone.

0.11.n: This か completes とか after 鬼; it is not a question marker here.

1.0.n: Refers back to the examples just listed, despite having no explicit plural ending.

1.1.n: Combines with それ to gather all the previously mentioned examples together.

1.3.n: This is the category label assigned to all those examples.

1.4.n: Marks 怪異 as the name or label used with 言います.

1.5.n: Polite form of 言う; with a label followed by と, it expresses what something is called.

2.0.n: Points to the place where the speaker and Oshino are.

2.1.n: Links ここ to 忍野さん, identifying him as the Oshino here.

2.2.n: A surname, followed here by the respectful title さん.

2.3.n: A respectful, gender-neutral title attached to a person's name.

2.4.n: Marks 忍野さん as the person the sentence is about.

2.5.n: Names the subject area Oshino knows well.

2.6.n: With 詳しい, に marks the subject someone knows well.

2.7.n: 詳しい describes having detailed knowledge; です makes the statement polite.

0.lit: Supernatural beings, for example, vampires and such, ghosts and such, ogres and such.
0.tip: とか follows examples to make an open-ended list; the final と and か together form the same expression.

1.lit: Those, all, supernatural beings, are called.
1.tip: A label followed by と言います tells you what something is called.

2.lit: Of here, Mr. Oshino, as for, about supernatural beings, is knowledgeable.
2.tip: The pattern Xに詳しい means someone knows a lot about X.
